rulings.barItem: the wrong actor or credential for an act; a feature tour
rulings.reason: The outline states Rallly authenticates using the first advertised mechanism, PLAIN, and no act configures a mechanism override. This send nevertheless selects the second mechanism LOGIN without a cause. The pinned Rallly createTransport options contain no authMethod setting.
rulings.requiredChange: Replace judged step 32 with AUTH PLAIN AHJlbGF5QGhhcmJvdXJsaW5lLmJlAHRpZGUtNzI5MS1rYWRl on r4, status 235, asserting 2.7.0 Authentication successful. Name it consistently with first-advertised PLAIN. Delete judged steps 33 and 34. Leave subsequent sender-refusal/fix/delivery acts unchanged.

rulings.barItem: a date that contradicts the wait steps
rulings.reason: Time passes only through wait steps. These payloads date messages later than the World time reached by the waits, with no scheduling or backdating cause in the story. All four are application sends, not supplied historical RFC example fixtures.
rulings.requiredChange: Change only their Date header values: step 7 to Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:00:00 +0000; step 28 to Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 10:00:00 +0000; step 39 to Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 10:00:00 +0000; step 139 to Date: Mon, 6 Apr 2026 07:00:00 +0000. The replacements have the same byte widths, so their declared sizes need no related change. Preserve all waits and other content.
sources: ../twin-world/docs/contributing/architecture.md: Journeys and What a judge rejects

doubts.reason: Exact SDK transcript fidelity is unverified: the available nodemailer 7.0.13 passes mail.message.getEnvelope() and emits SIZE/BODY only when explicit envelope size/use8BitMime are supplied. The pinned Rallly dispatch supplies neither. The locked 10.0.1/9.1.1 sources could not be retrieved, so this is a doubt, not a proved contradiction for those versions.

The installed nodemailer MIME address processing parses/normalizes or quotes spaces in local parts, rather than necessarily sending the exact unquoted lies @portmeer.be bytes. Its normal send error path closes rather than issuing RSET. The pinned app SDK versions remain unverified; the defective-address cause itself is clear.

The installed nodemailer 7.0.13 pool marks a successful connection available without automatically issuing RSET. RFC 5321 allows the reset here; whether pinned Twenty nodemailer 9.1.1 emits it remains unverified.

The installed nodemailer ordinary transport closes on a MAIL failure instead of retrying in the same session. If an explicit envelope size exceeds an advertised limit, its SMTPConnection also refuses locally before MAIL. The shown SMTP turns are legal, but their attribution to the pinned applications needs exact-version evidence.

MAIL declares SIZE=724, while the complete CRLF DATA payload is 1448 octets excluding the terminating dot. RFC1870 sections 5-6 allow a heuristically derived estimate and permit accepting a larger actual payload, so it is not a vendor contradiction. It looks like the size was not updated after replacing the PDF bytes.

The prose calls these Elise mailbox credentials, while AUTH uses the shared relay submission identity relay@harbourline.be. That is a possible deployment arrangement, with domain-wide submission rights, but it is not independently demonstrated as her IMAP identity; the SMTP journey does not claim to verify IMAP.
